title: Populate the JFRED repo with the canonical webapp + engine, then add it as a RevEng submodule
description:
Use subagents where possible for this task.  GOAL (decided 2026-07-16): JFRED is the COMPLETE, self-contained tool - anyone who clones it can (a) run the tool, (b) run `run-all-scenarios.py` to recreate the `.step_states` fixtures the engine relies on, (c) run `check_scenario_coverage` + the full test suite. The reconstruction engine goes PUBLIC with JFRED; RevEng keeps only its private value (scenario fixtures/ground-truth are already a submodule). This intentionally reverses task 57/59's 'engine stays private'.

STEPS (do in order, ship each before the next):
STEP 1 - ENGINE + WEBAPP: get the tool itself running standalone in JFRED - `webapp/` + `src/` engine + `viewer_server.ts` + `package.json` (`npm run app` serves 7343) + `LICENSE`. Verify `npm run app` works from a fresh clone with no jot present.
STEP 2 - RUN-ALL-SCENARIOS: bring the scenario test harness - `scenarios/` submodule + `run-all-scenarios.py` + `scenario-completeness-audit.py` + the vendored jot run-scenario slice (7 libs + SKILL.md + thin dispatcher + slimmed hooks.json) + tmux_lib (consolidated). Verify a cloner can regenerate `executed/.step_states` and `npm test`/`check_scenario_coverage` pass.
STEP 3 - FULLY STANDALONE, ZERO JOT: strip every remaining dependency on the jot plugin so JFRED needs nothing from `~/Programming/jot` or the installed plugin. Sweep for lingering `common.scripts` imports, hook paths, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` refs, hardcoded jot paths; add JFRED as a RevEng submodule and repoint `npm run app`/viewer_server to serve FROM it. Confirm with a clean-room clone that has jot uninstalled.

CANONICAL APP: the live tool is `webapp/` served at http://127.0.0.1:7343/ by `src/viewer_server.ts` (`/` -> `webapp/index.html`; `/app/*` -> `webapp/dist/` then `webapp/`). `jfred/jfred.html` (+ `api/*.js`, `web-shared/jfred-*`) is a SEPARATE, superseded frontend - do NOT ship it.

MANIFEST to put in JFRED:
- TOOL: `webapp/` (index.html, *.ts -> webapp/dist via tsconfig.webapp.json, views/, vendor/, styles.css) + `src/` (whole reconstruction engine + `viewer_server.ts`, backs `/api/config|projects|document|raw|blob|diff|range-patch|step-files`) + `package.json` (`npm run app`) + `LICENSE` (GPLv3). webapp compiles standalone (rootDir=webapp, zero `../src` imports) but the RUNNING site needs the engine endpoints, so the engine ships too.
- SCENARIOS: `scenarios/` (already a submodule, gitdir .git/modules/scenarios): 85 `.txt` + `scenario-generator/`. `executed/` is gitignored/generated (recreated by the runner).
- RUNNER: `run-all-scenarios.py` + `scenario-completeness-audit.py`. Drives a live Claude agent in a tmux pane via `/run-scenario`, polls for `executed/<stem>/.step_states/` + a `{"completed": true}` JSON.
- JOT run-scenario SLICE (the ONLY jot footprint - a closed 7-file graph, NOT the whole plugin): `skills/run-scenario/SKILL.md` + `common/scripts/{run_scenario_lib,bg_permissions_lib,claude_lib,hookjson_lib,tmux_lib,tmux_lib_internal,util_lib}.py`. Vendor them under the SAME `common/scripts/` path so their `from common.scripts.X import` lines need zero rewrites. Do NOT copy `jot_plugin_orchestrator.py` (it imports all of jot: jot_lib/todo/plate/debate/sync) - write a ~20-line dispatcher mapping the `/run-scenario` + `run-scenario-{launch,session-start,stop,session-end,execute,launch-and-execute,convert}` subcommands to run_scenario_lib functions. Slim `hooks/hooks.json` to just UserPromptSubmit -> that dispatcher. Completion signal: run_scenario_lib.py auto-installs a Stop hook into the DRIVEN agent (~line 301) pointing at `<dispatcher> run-scenario-stop <signal_dir>` and writes `.step_states/step-NNN/` + the completed JSON - repoint that `orchestrator_path` at the vendored dispatcher.
- TESTS: `tests/*.ts` incl. `check_scenario_coverage.test.ts` (read `scenarios/executed/`).

CONSOLIDATE: `tmux_lib` exists TWICE - RevEng top-level `tmux_lib/` (has pyproject.toml; `run-all-scenarios.py` does `from tmux_lib.tmux_lib import ...`) AND jot's `common/scripts/tmux_lib.py` (used by run_scenario_lib). Pick ONE or ship two drifting copies.

EXTERNAL PREREQS (README, can't vendor): Claude Code CLI installed+authed with a capable model (runner spawns a live agent; hardcoded model `claude-opus-4-6[1m]` -> make it a flag) - THE irreducible dep; plus tmux, python3, node+npm+tsx.

CLONER FLOW: `git clone --recursive && npm install` -> `python3 run-all-scenarios.py <tmux-pane>` (regenerates executed/.step_states; needs Claude+tmux) -> `npm test`. Note: `npm test`/check_scenario_coverage FAIL until `executed/` exists, so the runner step is mandatory first (optionally commit a fixture snapshot for people without Claude).

THEN: add JFRED as a git submodule of RevEng and repoint `npm run app`/viewer_server so 7343 serves FROM the submodule. Privacy gate: `git grep matkatmusicllc` = 0 hits in JFRED before first push. Downstream tasks 60 (demo JSONL), 61 (README), 62 (screenshots), 17/63 (Pages demo - needs a STATIC build; a server-backed webapp can't be static without a browser port of the engine, which is what jfred.html/api/*.js already were - revisit there), 64 (CI) target the JFRED repo.

STEP 2 DECISIONS (settled 2026-07-16, discussion in session d4542af6): (1) The '7-file jot slice' premise is STALE — 6 of the 7 common/scripts files in jot are SHIMS; the real implementations live in two PUBLIC repos already used as submodules by jot: github.com/matkatmusic/tmux_lib (tmux_lib.py, tmux_lib_internal.py) and github.com/matkatmusic/claude_plugin_lib (bg_permissions_lib, claude_lib, hookjson_lib, util_lib). The 'tmux_lib exists twice, consolidate' item DISSOLVES — both copies were the same repo all along. (2) JFRED gets THREE submodules: scenarios, external/tmux_lib, external/claude_plugin_lib. (3) Copy ONLY run_scenario_lib.py from jot into JFRED common/scripts/, editing its ~7 import lines to hit the submodules directly — NO shim/forwarding files. (4) Dispatcher = scripts/run_scenario_dispatcher.py (honest name, no 'jot' in the jot-free repo); patch the 3 orchestrator_path lines in the copied lib (176/284/1120) and give plugin_root a Path(__file__)-based fallback so no CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT env var is needed. (5) Skill + hook ship IN-REPO: .claude/skills/run-scenario/SKILL.md + UserPromptSubmit hook in .claude/settings.json (project-level, zero install; plugin-layout skills/ + hooks/hooks.json paths in the manifest above are WRONG for a plain repo). No install.sh needed so far. INTERIM until jfredToolsPlugin (task 108) replaces it. (6) Tests also need scripts/coverage_scenarios.ts (check_scenario_coverage.test.ts imports ../scripts/). (7) Related new tasks: 107 (replace the interim .claude run-scenario skill with the plugin version), 108 (jfredToolsPlugin: /run-scenario + /sync-jsonl-projects usable everywhere), 109 (jot removal), 110 (executed/ copy). /sync-jsonl-projects gets NO JFRED-local .claude copy — it stays in jot until the plugin.

title: Write the JFRED repo README (the actual pitch)
description: Write the JFRED repo's README (reframed 2026-07-15 for task 57's decision: public repo = JFRED, the static browser-only debugger — no Engine B, no npm). Outline: (1) hook — one sentence + hero screenshot: Claude Code's `/rewind` does NOT track changes made outside Claude (link https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing) — external edits, script runs, and git operations are invisible to checkpoints; JFRED reconstructs a session's file-change history from its JSONL transcript and file-history sidecar backups. (2) screenshots per item 62. (3) "How it works" — 3–4 paragraphs on JFReD's own model (the api/ scripts: transcript parsing, read/edit-stream extraction, snapshot store, edit replay, rewind classification; never fabricate — reconstruct only from evidence). Do NOT cite docs/engine-b-overview.md — Engine B stays private. (4) quick start: open `jfred/jfred.html` in a browser and load a JSONL (+ sidecar) — zero install. (5) honest scope notes: static, browser-only; what reconstruction can/can't recover. Screenshots land via item 62.

title: Capture JFRED README screenshots + stepper GIF
description: Capture JFRED README screenshots + GIF (reframed 2026-07-15: public repo = JFRED static debugger only — the webapp timeline / Diff-vs-Base / Details drawer are Engine-B private surfaces, dropped). Against the item-60 sample session, open `jfred/jfred.html` in the headless browse daemon and capture: (a) HERO: the three-pane PREVIOUS/COMPUTED/NEXT stepper mid-session; (b) the load screen with a JSONL loaded (line list populated); (c) a step showing a reconstructed file diff between panes. Plus one animated GIF stepping through revisions — worth more than all stills; record via screenshot sequence → `ffmpeg`/`gifski`. Light theme, consistent window size, no personal paths visible in any frame (the sample session's temp cwd will show — item 60 must make it neutral).
